text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS
- Some 20,000 Estonian families intend to buy a personal computer in the next year, a Baltic Media Facts poll reveals.
- The passenger ferry Normandie could not leave for Finland due to a failure in the bow visor operating system.
SONUMILEHT
- Parliament discussed a draft law on foreign relations, which was opposed by a number of members, who fear that the draft reduces parliament's role in foreign relations.
- The Bank of Estonia presented a tapestry to mark the fifth anniversary of the kroon.
- Top security and human rights body the OSCE extended its mission in Estonia until the end of 1997.
EESTI PAEVALEHT
- The transport ministry proposes establishing common railway stations with Russia on the Estonian border in Narva and Petseri.
- Prime Minister Mart Siimann visited the Oru peat fields in northeast Estonia before a government session.
POSTIMEES
- The main stage for the annual rock festival is being built at the Song Festival grounds. The event is to begin on June 14.
POSTIMEES
- Ex-Soviet officer Yevgeni Zobnin has been deported.
- A private farmer has begun to breed emus in Viljandi county in central Estonia. The exotic birds will be bred as poultry.
ARIPAEV
- The new owners of the Oru peat plant will begin production next week. They have contracts for 30,000 tonnes of peat.
- The ruling coalition parties have agreed to approve the law on advertising with an article banning tobacco advertisements.
-- Riga newsroom, +371 721 5240
